# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Brill_2015_midazolam"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Brill_2015_midazolam"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s11095-015-1752-9> (open access, PMC4628089)

The first study occasion of this cohort (the day of surgery) was published
separately as Brill 2014 and is packaged as `Brill_2014_midazolam`, where it
was pooled with healthy volunteers. The present model is a different fit: it
analyses both occasions of the 20 morbidly obese patients jointly, with
"bariatric surgery" as the covariate, and its structure (five transit
compartments, a second peripheral volume estimated as a fraction of the
first) and parameter values differ from the 2014 model.

# Population

Twenty morbidly obese adults (12 F / 8 M; age 26-57 years; body weight
112-186 kg, mean 144.4 kg; BMI 40-68 kg/m^2) undergoing laparoscopic
Roux-en-Y gastric bypass or sleeve gastrectomy at St. Antonius Hospital,
Nieuwegein, the Netherlands, received 7.5 mg oral midazolam followed by 5 mg
IV 160 +/- 48 min later on the day of surgery (occasion 1; the IV dose
coincided with induction of anaesthesia). Eighteen of them (16 gastric
bypass, 2 sleeve gastrectomy) returned 51.8 +/- 2.5 weeks later (occasion 2;
body weight 62-138 kg, mean 98.3 kg; mean weight loss 44.5 kg) and received
the same doses with the IV dose at 150 min. About 22 samples were taken per
patient per occasion (Brill 2015 Table I). The same information is available
from the model's `population` metadata.

# Source trace

All values are from the "Final model of simultaneous analysis" column of
Brill 2015 Table II.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|------:|-----------------|
| `lka_presurg` -- Ka = Ktr before surgery | log(0.117) 1/min | Table II, Ka = Ktr morbidly obese |
| `lka_postsurg` -- Ka = Ktr after surgery | log(0.267) 1/min | Table II, Ka = Ktr bariatric patients |
| `lfdepot` -- oral bioavailability | log(0.537) | Table II, F |
| `lcl` -- CL before surgery | log(0.385) L/min | Table II, CL morbidly obese |
| `e_prior_bariatric_cl` -- factor on CL after surgery | 1.68 | Table II, fCL bariatric patients (CL = 0.647 L/min) |
| `lq` -- Q before surgery | log(0.669) L/min | Table II, Q morbidly obese |
| `e_prior_bariatric_q` -- factor on Q after surgery | 3.22 | Table II, fQ bariatric patients (Q = 2.15 L/min) |
| `lq2` -- Q2 | log(0.551) L/min | Table II, Q2 |
| `lvc` -- Vc at 127 kg (before) / Vc (after) | log(37.3) L | Table II, Vmedian BW and Vcentral bariatric patients |
| `e_wt_vc` -- linear WT slope on Vc, before surgery | 0.0435 1/kg | Table II, X; Vc = Vmedian * (1 + X * (BW - 127)) |
| `lvp` -- Vp at 127 kg (before) / Vp (after) | log(106) L | Table II, Vmedian BW and V1st peripheral bariatric patients |
| `e_wt_vp` -- power WT exponent on Vp, before surgery | 3.93 | Table II, Y; Vp = Vmedian * (BW / 127)^Y |
| `lvp2` -- second peripheral volume | log(0.359 * 106) L | Table II, fV2nd peripheral = 0.359 of V1st peripheral |
| IIV Ka = Ktr | 42.4% CV | Table II |
| IIV CL | 19.7% CV | Table II |
| IIV F | 33.4% CV | Table II |
| IIV Vc | 53.7% CV | Table II |
| IIV V1st peripheral | 0 FIX | Table II |
| `propSd` -- proportional residual error | 0.421 | Table II, 42.1% |
| Five transit compartments, Ktr = Ka, MTT = (N + 1) / Ktr | n/a | Methods (absorption models); Results, Pharmacokinetic Analysis |
| Three-compartment disposition, Vp2 = fV * Vp | n/a | Results, Pharmacokinetic Analysis; Table II footnote |
| Binary covariate as P = Pp * Z^COV | n/a | Methods Eq. 3 |
| Weight effect only before surgery (Eqs. 6-8 with occasions switched) | n/a | Methods Eqs. 6-8; Results, Table II |
| Exponential IIV, proportional residual error | n/a | Methods Eqs. 1-2 |

# Derived quantities

The paper quotes the mean oral transit time MTT = (N + 1) / Ktr with N = 5 as
51.3 min before and 22.6 min after surgery, and the post-surgery CL and Q as
0.647 and 2.15 L/min. These follow from the packaged parameters exactly.

```{r derived}
mod <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Brill_2015_midazolam"))
p <- mod$theta
derived <- tibble::tibble(
  quantity = c("MTT before surgery (min)", "MTT after surgery (min)",
               "CL after surgery (L/min)", "Q after surgery (L/min)",
               "Vp2 (L)"),
  packaged = c(6 / exp(p[["lka_presurg"]]), 6 / exp(p[["lka_postsurg"]]),
               exp(p[["lcl"]]) * p[["e_prior_bariatric_cl"]],
               exp(p[["lq"]]) * p[["e_prior_bariatric_q"]],
               exp(p[["lvp2"]])),
  published = c(51.3, 22.6, 0.647, 2.15, 38)
)
knitr::kable(derived, digits = 3)
stopifnot(all(abs(derived$packaged / derived$published - 1) < 0.01))
```

# Replicating Figure 3

Brill 2015 Figure 3 shows the population mean and 90% interval of 1000
simulated patients given a 5 mg IV bolus, a 2.5 mg/h continuous infusion and
a 7.5 mg oral dose, for a morbidly obese patient (145 kg) before surgery and
for a patient after bariatric surgery. The paper simulated body weight from
the study distribution (144 +/- 26 kg); here weights are drawn from that
distribution and truncated to the observed pre-surgery range of 112-186 kg,
because the linear weight term on Vc becomes negative below 104 kg. After
surgery the volumes do not depend on weight, so the post-surgery arm uses the
typical post-surgery weight. Each arm has 200 virtual patients.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2015)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2015)
n_arm <- 200
cohort <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(
    id = seq_len(n_arm),
    WT = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_arm, 144, 26), 112), 186),
    PRIOR_BARIATRIC = 0,
    arm = "Before surgery"
  ),
  tibble::tibble(
    id = n_arm + seq_len(n_arm),
    WT = 98,
    PRIOR_BARIATRIC = 1,
    arm = "After surgery"
  )
)
typical <- tibble::tibble(
  id = 1:2, WT = c(145, 98), PRIOR_BARIATRIC = c(0, 1),
  arm = c("Before surgery", "After surgery")
)

make_events <- function(subjects, amt, cmt, obs_times, rate = 0) {
  dose <- subjects |>
    dplyr::mutate(time = 0, amt = amt, rate = rate, evid = 1, cmt = cmt)
  obs <- subjects |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = obs_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "central")
  dplyr::bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
    as.data.frame()
}

simulate_panel <- function(amt, cmt, obs_times, rate = 0) {
  vpc <- rxode2::rxSolve(
    mod, make_events(cohort, amt, cmt, obs_times, rate),
    keep = "arm", returnType = "data.frame"
  ) |>
    dplyr::group_by(arm, time) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      lo = quantile(Cc, 0.05), mid = median(Cc), hi = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(
    rxode2::zeroRe(mod), make_events(typical, amt, cmt, obs_times, rate),
    keep = "arm", returnType = "data.frame"
  )
  list(vpc = vpc, typical = typ)
}

plot_panel <- function(sim, title, caption) {
  ggplot(sim$vpc, aes(time, mid, colour = arm, fill = arm)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
    geom_line(data = sim$typical, aes(time, Cc, colour = arm),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, linewidth = 0.9) +
    labs(x = "Time (min)", y = "Midazolam (ng/mL)", colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
         title = title, caption = caption) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
}
```

## Figure 3a -- 5 mg IV bolus

```{r fig3a}
sim_iv <- simulate_panel(5000, "central", c(0, 1, 2, 5, seq(10, 800, by = 10)))
plot_panel(sim_iv, "5 mg IV bolus",
           "Replicates Figure 3a of Brill 2015. Lines: typical patient; band: 5th-95th percentile.") +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(1, 1000))
```

## Figure 3b -- 2.5 mg/h continuous infusion

```{r fig3b}
rate_ug_min <- 2500 / 60
sim_inf <- simulate_panel(rate_ug_min * 15000, "central",
                          seq(0, 15000, by = 100), rate = rate_ug_min)
plot_panel(sim_inf, "2.5 mg/h continuous IV infusion",
           "Replicates Figure 3b of Brill 2015.")
```

## Figure 3c -- 7.5 mg oral dose

```{r fig3c}
sim_po <- simulate_panel(7500, "depot", c(0, seq(1, 800, by = 1)))
plot_panel(sim_po, "7.5 mg oral dose",
           "Replicates Figure 3c of Brill 2015.")
```

## Steady state under the infusion

The infusion steady state is the dose rate divided by clearance, about 108 and
64 ng/mL before and after surgery, which are the plateaus of Figure 3b. The
paper states that steady state is reached in about 37 h before and about 14 h
after surgery; it does not say which fraction of steady state it used, so the
table gives the typical patient's time to 90% and 95% of steady state.

```{r steady-state}
css <- sim_inf$typical |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    css_closed_form = rate_ug_min / ifelse(dplyr::first(arm) == "After surgery",
                                           0.385 * 1.68, 0.385),
    conc_at_250h = dplyr::last(Cc),
    t90_h = time[which(Cc >= 0.90 * css_closed_form)[1]] / 60,
    t95_h = time[which(Cc >= 0.95 * css_closed_form)[1]] / 60,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(published_h = ifelse(arm == "Before surgery", 37, 14))
knitr::kable(css, digits = 2)
stopifnot(
  all(abs(css$conc_at_250h / css$css_closed_form - 1) < 0.01),
  all(css$published_h >= css$t90_h * 0.9 & css$published_h <= css$t95_h * 1.1)
)
```

# Both occasions in one patient

In the study each patient was observed before and again one year after
surgery, and the model shares one set of random effects across the two
occasions. A simulation of that design puts both occasions in one subject
record, with `PRIOR_BARIATRIC` and `WT` changing between them. The IV dose
follows the oral dose by 150 min, as on occasion 2. The study's occasions
were a year apart; here the second occasion starts two weeks (20,160 min)
after the first. Midazolam is eliminated completely within days, so the
shorter gap gives the same profiles, while integrating across a full year of
near-zero concentrations exceeds the ODE solver's default step limit and
returns missing values.

```{r both-occasions}
occ2_start <- 20160 # two weeks, in min
occ_times <- c(5, 15, 30, 45, 60, 75, 90, 120, 150,
               150 + c(5, 15, 30, 60, 90, 120, 150, 180, 240, 300))
n_pt <- 100
pts <- tibble::tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_pt),
  WT_pre = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_pt, 144.4, 21.7), 112), 186),
  WT_post = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_pt, 98.3, 18.0), 62), 138)
)
occasion_rows <- function(offset, post) {
  pts |>
    dplyr::mutate(WT = if (post == 1) WT_post else WT_pre,
                  PRIOR_BARIATRIC = post) |>
    tidyr::crossing(tibble::tibble(
      time = offset + c(0, 150, occ_times),
      amt = c(7500, 5000, rep(0, length(occ_times))),
      evid = c(1, 1, rep(0, length(occ_times))),
      cmt = c("depot", "central", rep("central", length(occ_times)))
    ))
}
ev_occ <- dplyr::bind_rows(occasion_rows(0, 0), occasion_rows(occ2_start, 1)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, evid, cmt, WT, PRIOR_BARIATRIC) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
  as.data.frame()

sim_occ <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_occ,
                           returnType = "data.frame") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    occasion = ifelse(PRIOR_BARIATRIC == 1, "After surgery", "Before surgery"),
    tad = ifelse(PRIOR_BARIATRIC == 1, time - occ2_start, time)
  )

sim_occ |>
  dplyr::group_by(occasion, tad) |>
  dplyr::summarise(lo = quantile(sim, 0.05), mid = median(sim),
                   hi = quantile(sim, 0.95), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(tad, mid, colour = occasion, fill = occasion)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after oral dose (min)", y = "Midazolam (ng/mL)",
       colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
       caption = paste("Study design of occasion 2 (7.5 mg oral, 5 mg IV at 150 min),",
                       "with residual error; compare with Figure 1 of Brill 2015.")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
```

# PKNCA validation

Non-compartmental analysis of the stochastic 7.5 mg oral simulation, grouped
by arm. Brill 2015 reports the oral Tmax of the Figure 3c population mean
curves (65 min before and 32 min after surgery) and a 1.5-fold higher Cmax
after surgery; the Cmax values in the reference column (30 and 43 ng/mL) were
read by the maintainers from the peaks of Figure 3c.

```{r pknca}
po_ind <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod, make_events(cohort, 7500, "depot", c(0, seq(1, 800, by = 1))),
  keep = "arm", returnType = "data.frame"
)
conc_po <- po_ind |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, arm)
dose_po <- cohort |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = 0, amt = 7500) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, arm)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_po, Cc ~ time | arm + id,
                             concu = "ng/mL", timeu = "min")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_po, amt ~ time | arm + id, doseu = "ug")
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 800, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                        auclast = TRUE)
nca_po <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj,
                                         intervals = intervals))

reference <- data.frame(
  arm = c("Before surgery", "After surgery"),
  cmax = c(30, 43),
  tmax = c(65, 32)
)
nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  nca_po, reference, by = "arm", params = c("cmax", "tmax"),
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", tmax = "min"),
  label_first_column = "NCA parameter"
)
```

```{r pknca-check}
med <- as.data.frame(nca_po$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(median = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median)
med
cmax_ratio <- med$cmax[med$arm == "After surgery"] / med$cmax[med$arm == "Before surgery"]
cmax_ratio
stopifnot(
  # Faster absorption after surgery: the median Tmax roughly halves.
  med$tmax[med$arm == "After surgery"] < 0.7 * med$tmax[med$arm == "Before surgery"],
  # The paper's 1.5-fold increase in Cmax, within the precision of a median.
  cmax_ratio > 1.2 && cmax_ratio < 1.8
)
```

The median simulated Tmax and Cmax track the published Figure 3c values. The
paper's Tmax and Cmax refer to the population mean of its own 1000-patient
simulation, so a difference of several minutes in Tmax is expected.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Covariate column.** The paper's binary covariate "bariatric surgery"
  (0 = occasion 1 before surgery, 1 = occasion 2 one year after) is carried
  as `PRIOR_BARIATRIC`. It changes within a subject between occasions, and
  `WT` should be the weight measured at each occasion.
* **Weight effects before surgery only.** Table II gives the weight
  equations for the morbidly obese occasion and the same Vmedian value,
  without weight terms, for the bariatric occasion; the Results state that
  the volumes after surgery showed no significant weight dependence. The
  model applies the weight terms only when `PRIOR_BARIATRIC = 0`. The linear
  term on Vc gives a negative volume for weights below 104 kg, outside the
  observed pre-surgery range (112-186 kg).
* **Second peripheral volume.** Table II estimates Vp2 as a fraction
  fV = 0.359 of Vp. Because Vp has no random effect, this is packaged
  exactly as `lvp2 = log(0.359 * 106)` with the same weight scaling as Vp.
  The table's annotation "*V 1st peripheral = 38 L" in this row is the
  resulting second peripheral volume (0.359 x 106 L = 38 L).
* **Table II annotation for fQ.** The row "fQ Bariatric patients 3.22
  (* Q Morbidly obese = 2.15)" is read as the post-surgery Q
  (0.669 x 3.22 = 2.15 L/min), consistent with the Results text "0.669 to
  2.15 L/min".
* **IIV scale.** The paper reports IIV as % CV without giving the formula;
  variances are `log(1 + CV^2)`, as in the other Leiden midazolam models in
  this package (`Brill_2014_midazolam`, `vanRongen_2015_midazolam`). The
  random effects are shared by both occasions because the paper reports no
  inter-occasion variability.
* **Bioavailability above 1.** Exponential IIV of 33.4% on F = 0.537 lets a
  few simulated patients (about 3%) have F > 1. The paper's Eq. 1 applies
  the exponential model to every parameter and gives no bound, so none is
  imposed.
* **Figure 3 cohort.** The paper's Monte Carlo simulation drew weight from
  144 +/- 26 kg; here the draw is truncated to 112-186 kg to keep Vc
  positive. Figure 3 cannot show whether the paper truncated.
* **Occasion 1 surgery.** On occasion 1 the IV dose coincided with induction
  of anaesthesia; the model has no term for anaesthesia or surgery, and the
  paper discusses this as a limitation.
